content.thinking:
With notice given 10 October by email, two months' written notice means the earliest end date is 10 December 2026, since under the Act tenant notice just needs to be at least two months without requiring alignment to the rental period. I'm treating the email as valid written notice and now considering what happens if the landlord agrees.

Other options include negotiating a shorter period, a surrender agreement, or finding a replacement tenant, but the landlord ultimately needs to decide, so I should flag this for approval. I won't make promises about the deposit since it's only returned after checkout with disputes going through ADR, and for keys I should avoid giving an address I don't know and just note arrangements will be made at the end of tenancy. The action here is to reply to the tenant, request landlord approval, and log a note — no ticket or further escalation needed beyond that approval request.

arguments.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job. 

Under the current rules (Renters' Rights Act, from 1 May 2026) a tenant needs to give two months' written notice, so one month isn't enough on its own. Taking your email as notice given today (10 October), the earliest your tenancy can end is 10 December 2026. Your rent stays payable until then.

You can leave sooner only if your landlord agrees in writing. We're asking him now whether he'll accept 10 November. I can't promise the answer, so please don't treat 10 November as agreed until we confirm it in writing. Helping find a new tenant may make agreement more likely.

Keys: please don't drop them anywhere yet. We'll confirm the handover place and time once your end date is settled. Handing keys back doesn't end the tenancy by itself.

Deposit: your deposit is protected with mydeposits. It is dealt with after the tenancy ends and the flat has been checked, and we'll write to you about this nearer the time. Any disagreement about deductions can go to the scheme's free dispute service.

Kind regards,
Lettings team

options: Recommended: hold to 10 Dec 2026 unless a replacement tenant is found, then agree a surrender early in writing
Agree in writing to 10 Nov 2026 as requested
Agree another date between 10 Nov and 10 Dec

arguments.note: 10 Oct 2026: tenant emailed one month's notice for 10 Nov. Treated as notice given 10 Oct; earliest valid end 10 Dec 2026. Landlord asked about early surrender; tenant told not agreed yet. Deposit £2019 (mydeposits) not to be released until tenancy ends and checkout done.

answers.question: Is the notice valid as given? Earliest end date?
answers.answer: No. Tenants must give two months' written notice. Treating the email as written notice received 10 Oct 2026, the earliest end date is 10 Dec 2026. The 10 Nov date is not valid unless the landlord agrees in writing.

answers.question: What options exist to end sooner?
answers.answer: The landlord can agree in writing to a shorter notice period or a surrender, for example 10 Nov or a date in between. A replacement tenant could make this more likely. The agency cannot agree it, because the decision is the landlord's.

answers.question: What do you reply and what do you start?
answers.answer: I replied to Tom with the 10 Dec date, the early-release option, a note that keys should be held until handover is arranged, and how the deposit works (mydeposits, returned after the tenancy ends and a check, disputes go to the scheme's ADR). I requested landlord approval (APR-102) and added a record note. No repair ticket was needed. Handover details and the deposit return are to be confirmed later.

arguments.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job. 

Under the current rules (Renters' Rights Act, from 1 May 2026) a tenant needs to give two months' written notice, so one month isn't enough on its own. Taking your email as notice given today (10 October), the earliest your tenancy can end is 10 December 2026. Your rent stays payable until then.

You can leave sooner only if your landlord agrees in writing. We're asking him now whether he'll accept 10 November. I can't promise the answer, so please don't treat 10 November as agreed until we confirm it in writing. Helping find a new tenant may make agreement more likely.

Keys: please don't drop them anywhere yet. We'll confirm the handover place and time once your end date is settled. Handing keys back doesn't end the tenancy by itself.

Deposit: your deposit is protected with mydeposits. It is dealt with after the tenancy ends and the flat has been checked, and we'll write to you about this nearer the time. Any disagreement about deductions can go to the scheme's free dispute service.

Kind regards,
Lettings team

answers.question: Is the notice valid as given? Earliest end date?
answers.answer: No. Tenants must give two months' written notice. Treating the email as written notice received 10 Oct 2026, the earliest end date is 10 Dec 2026. The 10 Nov date is not valid unless the landlord agrees in writing.

answers.question: What options exist to end sooner?
answers.answer: The landlord can agree in writing to a shorter notice period or a surrender, for example 10 Nov or a date in between. A replacement tenant could make this more likely. The agency cannot agree it, because the decision is the landlord's.
